subject: CareCrest follow-up: deployment mode qualification & compliance asks
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: CareCrest follow-up: deployment mode qualification & compliance asks

Hi Sarah — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call plus the asks we discussed so we’re aligned on next steps.

Call summary (short)
- Primary requirement: CareCrest will be processing PHI for the pilot; customer requires a BAA and SOC2 Type II evidence before production.
- Preference discussed: private VPC or on-prem if needed for audit/regulatory reasons; alternate paths are Dedicated reserved capacity or Hosted API with BAA + additional controls.
- Timeline: target pilot start late Feb; security review slated for mid-Jan.

Technical clarifications we need from your security team
1) Confirm whether PHI will be stored persistently in our service or only passed transiently (e.g., tokenized/ephemeral).
2) Encryption key requirements — do you require a customer-managed KMS/HSM or is provider-managed KMS acceptable for the pilot?
3) Logging and retention needs — what retention period do you need for audit logs (default we provide 1 year; longer retention is possible but impacts cost).
4) Audit windows — will you be requesting on-site/remote evidence for a regulatory audit in the next 12 months?

Internal notes / recommended routes (for CareCrest)
- Hosted + BAA: fastest to production if SOC2 attestation + additional controls (regional isolation, restricted dev access) are acceptable to CareCrest.
- Dedicated capacity: predictable throughput and stronger isolation, good middle ground for pilot if they want a managed environment without on-prem ops.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full isolation and customer control over keys/networking — recommended if CareCrest requires HSM or strict data residency/air-gap requirements.

Attachments: redwood-hosting-options-summary.pdf — short comparison of tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Next steps (proposed)
- Sarah: confirm PHI at-rest expectations and provide your security contact (name/email) who will own evidence requests.
- Redwood: share SOC2 Type II redacted attestation, BAA template, and a deployment-option cost delta for Dedicated vs Private.
- Schedule 30-min security deep-dive next week with CareCrest security team.

Thanks — I’ll assemble a short evidence packet once I have your security contact.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@carecrest.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:23:00 -0500
Subject: Re: CareCrest follow-up: deployment mode qualification & compliance asks

Thanks Rishi — solid recap. Quick answers from our side and a couple of asks before we schedule the security call.

Clarifications
- PHI: yes — pilot will include patient identifiers and clinical notes that must be treated as PHI at rest for the pilot. We will require a signed BAA for any environment that stores PHI persistently.
- KMS: for pilot we are open to provider-managed KMS if you can demonstrate encryption at rest with customer separation; for production we may require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key / HSM).
- Logs/retention: we need 3 years of immutable audit logs for actions that access PHI (minimum). Can Redwood provide this retention OR an export mechanism into our SIEM?
- Audit: we expect at least one compliance audit in the next 12 months (remote preferred). We’ll need evidence (SOC2 Type II report) and a contact who can respond to evidence requests.

Security contact
- Please loop in: Jordan Reyes (security@carecrest.ai) — will own the evidence review.

Documents we need from Redwood before the security call
1) SOC2 Type II attestation (redacted OK)
2) BAA template for review
3) Short deployment options matrix showing which features are available on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (networking, KMS, audit logs, retention, region guarantees)

Timing: Jordan is available Thurs 18 Jan (10–11am EST) or Mon 22 Jan (2–3pm EST) for a 30–45 minute call.

Also: can you include a rough cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for a small pilot (1–2 GPUs reserved)? That will help us pre-clear procurement.

Appreciate it — Sarah
Sarah Miller
Head of Product Ops — CareCrest Health
sarah.miller@carecrest.ai

Thanks Sarah — looping in procurement/solutions notes.

> On Wed, Jan 11, 2028 at 9:23 AM Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@carecrest.ai> wrote:
> > PHI: yes — pilot will include patient identifiers and clinical notes that must be treated as PHI at rest for the pilot. We will require a signed BAA for any environment that stores PHI persistently.

We can provide the SOC2 Type II (redacted) and our standard BAA template for review. For the pilot:
- Recommendation: start on Dedicated capacity in us-west region for the pilot (reserved GPUs) — gives stronger isolation and simpler KMS options while keeping time-to-value short.
- If CareCrest requires BYOK/HSM for production, we can plan Private VPC/on-prem for later; we will surface realistic timelines and delta cost for that migration.

Cost delta (very rough, ballpark for pilot)
- Hosted (with BAA + SOC2 controls): baseline API usage costs + minimal setup — lowest cost and fastest.
- Dedicated (1–2 GPU nodes reserved): +approx $X,XXX/mo (includes reserved capacity and basic support hours) — predictable throughput and isolation.
- Private VPC / on-prem: one-time onboarding + infra + higher monthly ops — we will provide exact quotes after we scope network and HSM needs.

Action items we’ll take now
1) Share SOC2 (attached) and standard BAA template in a single packet.
2) Prepare a short comparison matrix by EOW showing the KMS, logging, and retention differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
3) Draft a (non-binding) pilot cost delta for 1–2 GPU Dedicated vs Hosted and attach to the packet.

Rishi — I’ll own the evidence packet assembly and the cost ballpark. Sarah/Jordan — please confirm which day/time works for the security call and whether Jordan needs any pre-reads.

—Marissa
